feedback: The candidate correctly encodes the safety task 'never both take the key and have the ball moved away' as the negated conjunction G(~has_door_key | ~blocker_moved). Strengths: (1) Semantic fidelity — the violation guard `has_door_key & blocker_moved` uses only condition propositions and fires exactly when both hold on the same labeled step, matching the domain's own 'never hold together' phrasing; `blocker_moved` is rightly treated as a persistent condition (not latched), so dropping the ball back in front of the door restores safety-check consistency. (2) Violation reachability — the forbidden state is genuinely attainable (pick up ball, drop it away from the door cell, then pick up the key, e.g. trace seed 0 shape), so the -1.0 penalty is non-vacuous and the task is non-trivial. (3) Structure — u1 is an absorbing violation state, correctly making a single violation permanently fail a 'never' task; no regression back to u0 is needed or desired. u0 is declared in STATES, listed in FINAL_STATES, and is the accepting state for a safety task (a safe episode stays in u0 throughout and terminates there; a violating episode ends in non-accepting u1). (4) Coverage and determinism — the transition function is total and deterministic: u0 has the specific guard plus an else self-loop, u1 has an else self-loop, so all irrelevant propositions (door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost) and event/condition distinctions are correctly absorbed without misuse of the key_lost event. (5) Reward safety — a single bounded -1.0 on the violating transition and 0 elsewhere gives maximal return for any violation-free behavior; no dense progress rewards are needed for a pure constraint task and none are present, so there is no incentive conflict or unbounded/farmed reward. (6) Compactness — 2 states is minimal for a violation flag. (7) Format — all required headers present in the paper's layout (REWARD_MACHINE, STATES, INITIAL_STATE, nonempty FINAL_STATES, TRANSITION_FUNCTION, REWARD_FUNCTION), with reward given on the (state, event, next-state) triple. Minor non-blocking note: only the first violation is penalized (subsequent steps in u1 fall under the zero-reward else loop); this does not affect optimal behavior, since any optimal policy avoids the first violation entirely.
